title: Neural evidence supports a novel framework for spatial navigation

findings.antecedent: Traditional three-category framework (landmark, route, survey knowledge)
findings.consequent: Understanding of brain mechanisms for spatial navigation
findings.quote: recent neuroimaging studies that such a classification system is not adequate for understanding the brain.

findings.consequent: Activation of multiple brain regions (hippocampus, parahippocampal gyrus, caudate, retrosplenial cortex)
findings.quote: Scans during the tests revealed that both tasks activated multiple brain regions, including the hippocampus, parahippocampal gyrus, caudate, and retrosplenial cortex. Importantly, this result suggests that multiple aspects of a neural network are activated when performing navigational tasks, and that route and survey knowledge do not necessarily have distinct neural correlates.

findings.consequent: Parahippocampus activity
findings.quote: The parahippocampus appears to be involved in view-based scene recognition.

findings.consequent: PET activation of parahippocampal gyrus (including perirhinal, entorhinal cortices) vs. hippocampus
findings.quote: This landmark task showed increased PET activation of the parahippocampal gyrus (which includes the parahippocampal, perirhinal, and entorhinal cortices), but not the hippocampus, as compared with baseline.

findings.antecedent: Scenes and landmarks presented in spatial context vs. faces and objects in isolation
findings.consequent: fMRI activity in parahippocampal cortex and nearby fusiform gyrus (PPA)
findings.quote: The parahippocampal cortex and nearby fusiform gyrus (together often referred to as the "parahippocampal place area" or PPA) also show increased fMRI activity for scenes and landmarks presented in spatial context relative to faces and objects presented in isolation.

findings.consequent: fMRI adaptation effects in parahippocampal cortex when observing different views of the same place
findings.quote: participants with greater navigational ability showed larger fMRI adaptation effects in the parahippocampal cortex when observing different views of the same place.

findings.consequent: Difficulty identifying a location when task relies on short-term memory and integrating across different viewpoints
findings.quote: patients with hippocampal damage but intact parahippocampi have been shown to have difficulty identifying a location when the task relies on short-term memory and involves integrating across different viewpoints.

findings.consequent: Difficulty with all tasks requiring viewpoint-independent identification
findings.quote: Patients with damage to perirhinal areas had difficulty with all tasks requiring viewpoint-independent identification.

findings.consequent: Global activation in the hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus
findings.quote: The results showed that boundary learning did in fact promote global activation in the hippocampus. The parahippocampal gyrus also appeared to be activated during learning relative to boundaries.

findings.antecedent: Imagining scenes with walls or boundaries vs. complex scenes without
findings.consequent: Left hippocampus activity
findings.quote: the left hippocampus is active when imagining scenes with walls or boundaries, as compared with equally complex scenes consisting of towers.

findings.antecedent: Accuracy in locating a target relative to enclosure boundaries
findings.consequent: Hippocampal and parahippocampal theta oscillations
findings.quote: hippocampal and parahippocampal theta oscillations are correlated with accuracy in locating a target relative to the boundaries of the enclosure.

findings.consequent: Greater response in posterior parahippocampal cortex vs. anterior region
findings.quote: spatial contexts producing a greater response in the posterior parahippocampal cortex, and nonspatial contexts, a greater response in the anterior region.

findings.antecedent: Previously seen isolated objects vs. novel objects
findings.consequent: Hippocampus activation
findings.quote: the hippocampus showed increased activation to previously seen isolated objects over novel objects, whereas the parahippocampus did not, indicating that the hippocampus is sensitive to familiarity, consistent with its role in incidental learning.

findings.consequent: Hippocampal activation
findings.quote: hippocampal activation was correlated with spatial components of learning, whereas activity in the parahippocampal gyrus was correlated with contextual learning during a navigation task.

findings.antecedent: Lesions to perirhinal and postrhinal regions in rats
findings.consequent: Acquisition of contextual associations regarding fear
findings.quote: Lesions to the perirhinal and postrhinal regions of the parahippocampal area in rats prevent the acquisition of contextual associations regarding fear.

findings.antecedent: Lesions to hippocampus proper in rats
findings.consequent: Place learning in Morris water maze
findings.quote: lesions to the hippocampus proper do affect place learning.

findings.antecedent: Initial navigation to a target relative to three landmarks
findings.consequent: Activity in hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus, and accuracy of subsequent retrieval of target location
findings.quote: Increased activity in the hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus during initial navigation to a target relative to three landmarks was correlated with more accurate subsequent retrieval of the target location.

findings.antecedent: Scene in a larger context (e.g., labeled location) vs. isolated scenes
findings.consequent: Retrosplenial cortex activation vs. parahippocampal gyrus BOLD signal
findings.quote: the retrosplenial cortex had preferential activation for a scene in a larger context, such as when the location was labeled.

findings.consequent: Retrosplenial cortex treating different views of a scene as the same (fMRI attenuation)
findings.quote: The retrosplenial cortex may also treat different views of a scene as being the same when viewed with continuous movement, as evidenced by fMRI attenuation.

findings.consequent: Retrosplenial cortex sensitivity (fMRI adaptation) vs. parahippocampal cortex sensitivity
key_citations: Dilks, Julian, Kubilius, Spelke, and Kanwisher, 2011
findings.quote: the retrosplenial cortex was sensitive to mirror reversals of scenes, measured by fMRI adaptation, while the parahippocampal cortex was not.

findings.consequent: Activity in hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus
findings.quote: The route description task increased activity in the hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus, and also produced more activation in the hippocampus than did the landmark task.

findings.consequent: Hippocampus activity and accuracy in learning sequences
findings.quote: the hippocampus has also been associated with both the encoding and retrieval of nonspatial sequences, and it tends to be correlated with accuracy in learning sequences... and especially with distinguishing between overlapping sequences.

findings.antecedent: Learning longer routes through a maze vs. shorter routes
findings.consequent: Increased theta rhythm activity
findings.quote: Increased theta rhythm activity was observed when learning longer routes through a maze than when learning shorter routes.

findings.antecedent: Violation of expectations about next object in a learned sequence
findings.consequent: Hippocampal activity
findings.quote: Kumaran and Maguire (2006) found increased hippocampal activity when expectations were violated about the next object in a learned sequence of objects, suggesting that the hippocampus might play a role in predicting sequential events and detecting mismatches.

findings.antecedent: Damage to parahippocampus or nearby lingual and fusiform gyri
findings.consequent: Difficulty identifying suitable navigation landmarks and learning new locations from visual memory
findings.quote: Patients with damage to the parahippocampus or the nearby lingual and fusiform gyri have difficulty identifying landmarks suitable for navigation, as well as difficulty learning new locations from visual memory.

findings.antecedent: Free exploration of a maze and subsequent retrieval of routes
findings.consequent: Parahippocampal cortex activation
findings.quote: parahippocampal cortex activation occurs during free exploration of a maze and subsequent retrieval of routes between locations, with similar levels of activation throughout the learning and retrieval processes.

findings.antecedent: Viewing objects at decision points on unfamiliar routes vs. other objects along the route
findings.consequent: Parahippocampal gyrus global activation
findings.quote: After learning a route, the parahippocampal gyrus shows greater global activation when viewing objects located at decision points on the route than when viewing other objects along the route.

findings.consequent: Decision point effects in parahippocampal gyrus
findings.quote: this result only holds for routes in unfamiliar areas; routes in well-known areas produce no such decision point effects.

findings.consequent: Activity in parahippocampal gyrus at decision points
findings.quote: Weniger et al. (2010) found that the activity in the parahippocampal gyrus at decision points decreases as the route becomes more familiar.

findings.antecedent: Reliance on spatial relations (object-distal landmarks) vs. ordinal/response strategy (e.g., 'take third arm')
findings.consequent: BOLD signal in hippocampus vs. caudate nucleus during learning
key_citations: Iaria, Petrides, Dagher, Pike, and Bohbot, 2003
findings.quote: Individuals who relied on spatial relations between the object and distal landmarks had an increase in the BOLD signal in the hippocampus during learning, whereas those who relied on an ordinal or response strategy... showed activity in the caudate nucleus.

findings.consequent: Errors in navigation
key_citations: Iaria, Petrides, Dagher, Pike, and Bohbot, 2003
findings.quote: Ordinal learners also made fewer errors, suggesting that a nonspatial strategy may be more reliable in this situation.

findings.consequent: Gray matter density in hippocampus vs. caudate nucleus
findings.quote: Spatial learners tended to have a greater gray matter density in the hippocampus, whereas ordinal learners had a greater density in the caudate nucleus.

findings.antecedent: Navigation based on actions at a local landmark
findings.consequent: Activity in dorsal striatum (caudate head)
findings.quote: Participants who learned to navigate to a location on the basis of actions at a local landmark showed increased activity in the dorsal striatum, in particular at the head of the caudate.

findings.antecedent: Preference for place-learning strategies (taking novel shortcuts)
findings.consequent: Activation in hippocampus during encoding
findings.quote: Those who preferred place learning exhibited greater activation in the hippocampus during encoding.

findings.antecedent: Preference for response strategies (following known route)
findings.consequent: Activation in caudate
findings.quote: those who used a response strategy showed more activation in the caudate, regardless of their accuracy in the task.

findings.antecedent: Selective damage to caudate nucleus (Huntington's patients)
findings.consequent: Impaired performance on route task (compensated by increased hippocampal activity)
findings.quote: Huntington's patients with selective damage to the caudate nucleus do not show impaired performance on a route task, for they are apparently able to compensate with increased activity in the hippocampus.

findings.antecedent: Finding novel paths between known locations in a virtual town
findings.consequent: BOLD response in parahippocampal cortex, posterior parietal cortex, and caudate body
findings.quote: finding novel paths between known locations in a virtual town leads to an increased BOLD response in the parahippocampal cortex, posterior parietal cortex, and caudate body.

findings.consequent: Caudate body activity
findings.quote: repeating a well-known route yields an increase in the caudate body only.

findings.consequent: Hippocampus activity
findings.quote: Participants who were more accurate at wayfinding also showed increased activity in the hippocampus.

findings.consequent: Activity in head of caudate during route-following task
findings.quote: those who were less accurate at wayfinding had more activity in the head of the caudate during the route-following task.

findings.antecedent: Route knowledge consolidation into response-based process
findings.consequent: Parietal cortex and caudate involvement
findings.quote: as route knowledge becomes consolidated into a more purely response-based process, the parietal cortex and caudate become more involved.

findings.antecedent: Response-based trials vs. place-based trials (star-shaped radial maze)
findings.consequent: Left hippocampus activity vs. right hippocampus activity
key_citations: Igloi, Doeller, Berthoz, Rondi-Rieg and Burgess, 2010
findings.quote: the left hippocampus was active during response-based trials, whereas the right hippocampus was responsive during place trials.

findings.antecedent: Making decisions about goals and associated actions in partially overlapping routes vs. nonoverlapping routes
findings.consequent: Activity in hippocampus and parahippocampal cortex
key_citations: Brown, Ross, Keller, Hasselmo, and Stern, 2010
findings.quote: Brown, Ross, Keller, Hasselmo, and Stern (2010) found increased activity in both the hippocampus and parahippocampal cortex while participants made decisions about goals and the associated actions in partially overlapping, as compared to nonoverlapping, routes.

findings.consequent: Positively correlated functional connectivity between hippocampus and caudate
findings.quote: Brown, Ross, Tobyne, and Stern (2012) found positively correlated functional connectivity between the hippocampus and caudate when participants distinguished between overlapping routes, suggesting that these regions are both important for graph learning.

findings.antecedent: Making decisions about where to explore in a 2-D spatial memory task
findings.consequent: Subsequent retrieval and hippocampus activity
key_citations: Voss, Gonsalves, Federmeier, Tranel, and Cohen, 2011
findings.quote: making decisions about where to explore in a 2-D spatial memory task improved subsequent retrieval and was correlated with activity in the hippocampus.

findings.antecedent: Volitional control of movement and exploratory behavior
findings.consequent: Hippocampal theta rhythm activity
findings.quote: Volitional control of movement and exploratory behavior is also associated with increased hippocampal theta rhythm activity.

findings.consequent: Increased activity in hippocampus (bilateral), left parahippocampal cortex, retrosplenial cortex, lateral and medial prefrontal cortex
findings.quote: Spiers and Maguire (2006) observed increased activity, relative to a coasting baseline, in the hippocampus bilaterally, as well as in the left parahippocampal cortex, the retrosplenial cortex, and the lateral and medial prefrontal cortex during sections of the taxi ride in which drivers planned the route to the goal.

findings.consequent: Larger posterior hippocampal areas
findings.quote: Taxi drivers also have larger posterior hippocampal areas, correlated with their numbers of years on the job, than do either controls... or bus drivers.

findings.consequent: Faster times navigating to a goal
findings.quote: Microstructural integrity in the hippocampus is correlated with faster times navigating to a goal.

findings.antecedent: Navigating toward a destination in a familiar environment vs. simply following a path
findings.consequent: Greater regional cerebral blood flow in right hippocampus
findings.quote: Using PET, the right hippocampus has been shown to have greater regional cerebral blood flow when navigating toward a destination in a familiar environment than when simply following a path.

findings.consequent: BOLD hippocampal activity
findings.quote: BOLD hippocampal activity increases with proximity to the goal.

findings.consequent: fMRI activity in retrosplenial cortex
findings.quote: In a route-learning task, Wolbers et al. (2004) found increased fMRI activity in the retrosplenial cortex during encoding as compared to baseline.

findings.consequent: Retrosplenial activity
findings.quote: The retrosplenial cortex showed performance-related increases in activity with each encoding session, such that the more information the participant acquired about the maze, the greater the retrosplenial activity.

findings.antecedent: Amount of spatial layout learning (graph information)
findings.consequent: Hippocampal activity
findings.quote: Hippocampal activity was correlated with the amount of spatial layout learning that took place on a given time through the route.

findings.consequent: Confusion regarding heading direction
findings.quote: Damage to this area has been associated with confusion regarding heading direction.

findings.consequent: Cells in rat postsubiculum and entorhinal cortex sensitivity
findings.quote: Cells in the rat postsubiculum and entorhinal cortex are sensitive to heading direction.

findings.consequent: Regions in parietal cortex and entorhinal cortex activity
findings.quote: In humans, regions that respond to particular heading directions are found in parietal cortex... while grid cells... and cells sensitive to heading direction... are found in the entorhinal cortex.

findings.consequent: Hippocampal theta rhythm modulation
findings.quote: The hippocampal theta rhythm is modulated by the visual speed of the navigator and may be relevant for spatial updating relative to the other objects in the environment.

findings.antecedent: Locations near each other in physical space vs. farther apart
findings.consequent: fMRI adaptation in hippocampus
findings.quote: the hippocampus showed greater fMRI adaptation for locations that were near each other in physical space than for locations that were farther apart.

findings.consequent: Activity in hippocampus, entorhinal cortex, and subiculum
key_citations: Viard, Doeller, Hartley, Bird, and Burgess, 2011
findings.quote: increased activity in the hippocampus with proximity to the goal, while Spiers and Maguire (2007a) found that activity in the entorhinal cortex and subiculum was correlated with goal proximity.

findings.antecedent: Accuracy on relative distance judgments between objects
findings.consequent: Global neural activity in hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus
findings.quote: the accuracy on relative distance judgments between objects was correlated with global neural activity in both the hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus.

findings.antecedent: Survey encoding from a bird's-eye perspective
findings.consequent: Activation of bilateral fusiform and inferior temporal gyri and posterior superior parietal cortex, but no activation in hippocampus or parahippocampal cortex
findings.quote: survey encoding from a bird's-eye perspective activated the bilateral fusiform and inferior temporal gyri and the posterior superior parietal cortex, but they found no activation in the hippocampus or parahippocampal cortex as compared to fixation.

findings.antecedent: Damage to hippocampus and entorhinal cortex
findings.consequent: Performance on most path integration tasks
findings.quote: patients with damage to the hippocampus and entorhinal cortex are able to perform most path integration tasks at the same level as controls.

findings.consequent: Mental imagery involvement
findings.quote: Path integration tasks rely on mental imagery... which is also supported in the hippocampus.

findings.consequent: Difficulty producing descriptions of objects and spatial relations in novel imagined experience
findings.quote: Patients with hippocampal damage have difficulty producing descriptions of both objects and spatial relations in a novel imagined experience.

findings.antecedent: Making spatial decisions from memory vs. direct perception
findings.consequent: Increased BOLD signal in parahippocampal gyrus
findings.quote: The parahippocampal gyrus also shows an increased BOLD signal when making spatial decisions from memory rather than from direct perception... suggesting a possible role in performing mental imagery.

findings.consequent: Activity in frontal regions (dorsolateral prefrontal cortex)
findings.quote: frontal areas, especially the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, are associated with working memory... and some studies have found activity in frontal regions during spatial learning.

findings.antecedent: Damage to ventral medial prefrontal cortex
findings.consequent: Difficulty keeping navigational goals in mind
findings.quote: A case study has revealed that a patient with damage to the ventral medial prefrontal cortex had difficulty keeping navigational goals in mind.

findings.antecedent: Closer proximity to navigational goal and taking detours to a goal
findings.consequent: Increased activity in medial prefrontal cortex
findings.quote: Medial prefrontal cortex also shows increased activity with closer proximity to the navigational goal... and with taking detours to a goal, indicating that the prefrontal cortex may mediate goal-oriented navigation.
